newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Six Irianese killed in Indonesia tribal clash.
newsitem.headline: Six Irianese killed in Indonesia tribal clash.

text.p: Six people were killed and more than 60 injured when thousands of Indonesian tribesmen armed with poison-tipped arrows and machetes clashed in eastern Irian Jaya province after an alleged rape, police said on Tuesday.
More than 2,000 people from the Amungme and Dani tribes fought near the mining town of Tembagapura, some 4,000 km (2,500 miles) east of Jakarta, on Sunday and Monday.
But police and residents said the situation had returned to normal on Tuesday following a meeting between the two tribes.

Police said the clash was sparked by the alleged rape of a Dani woman by an Amungme in a village about four km (2.5 miles) from Tembagapura, where PT Freeport Indonesia operates one of the world's largest copper and gold mines.
Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States owns 81.28 percent of Freeport Indonesia, with the Indonesian government and PT Indocopper Investama holding a 9.36-percent stake each.
Freeport Indonesia spokesman Ed Pressman said mining operations had not been affected by the clash.
"Our operations were not affected in any way by the incident," he told Reuters in Jakarta. "I have not heard of any employees staying away from work."
The police official said the Dani tribesmen had asked the Amungme for 2,030,000 rupiah ($855) in compensation, but the demand was rejected, sparking the clashes.
"More than 2,000 tribespeople clashed on Sunday and Monday," he said. "They were armed with ordinary and poison-tipped arrows, stones and machetes."
"Six people were killed, while 61 were injured, eight of them seriously," he added.
Residents said the clash between the Dani and Amungme tribes was the latest in a series stretching over several hundred years as they fought over fertile farming land.
"The Amungme have always been the smaller tribe and have been displaced by the Dani from fertile land for centuries," one said. "The reasons for the latest clash are much the same."
Residents said the Dani tribespeople had been migrating to villages around Tembagapura in search of better living conditions.
